articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative routes are available for step-free access to platforms.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 20 August 2026, impacting accessibility for passengers. The lift has been unavailable since 5:38pm on that date, and there is no specified date for when it will be repaired.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, but must cross the tracks to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has advised that they are sorry for any inconvenience caused by this disruption. Passengers are encouraged to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes if necessary.

Further updates regarding the lift's status will be provided as they become available. For more information, passengers can check the Transport for Greater Manchester website.

articles.title: Zac Kennard-Kettle to Referee Rochdale's Match Against Crawley Town
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's first home game back in the EFL will see Zac Kennard-Kettle officiating, following in the footsteps of his father, Trevor Kettle.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's upcoming match against Crawley Town on Saturday will be officiated by referee Zac Kennard-Kettle. This match marks Dale's first home game since their return to the English Football League (EFL).

Zac Kennard-Kettle is the son of Trevor Kettle, a well-known referee who retired from the National List four years ago. Fans will be keen to see how Zac performs in this significant fixture for the club.

The match is expected to draw a strong local crowd as supporters look forward to the return of EFL football at Spotland Stadium.

As the game approaches, both teams will be preparing to secure vital points early in the season.

articles.title: Kirkstall Avenue Roadworks Scheduled for 6 November 2026 in Littleborough
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that Kirkstall Avenue in Littleborough will be temporarily closed for roadworks on 6 November 2026, affecting local traffic and access.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that part of Kirkstall Avenue in Littleborough will be temporarily closed on 6 November 2026. The closure will extend 34 metres from the junction with Tintern Avenue and will continue for 23 metres in a south-westerly direction.

During this period, no waiting will be permitted in the closed section of the road at any time. This closure may impact local traffic and access to nearby roads, including Shore Road, Furness Avenue, and Tintern Avenue.

Residents and motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and seek alternative routes where possible. The council has provided a map of the roadworks, which can be accessed through their website.

Further updates regarding the roadworks and any potential changes will be communicated by Rochdale Borough Council as the date approaches.

articles.title: Rochdale Commemorates Comedian Jimmy Cricket Ahead of Funeral
articles.excerpt: Rochdale will pay tribute to comedian Jimmy Cricket, who passed away on August 3, with a vigil and funeral service this week.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will have the opportunity to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral this week. Jimmy Cricket, known for his clean humour and catchphrase 'And there’s more', died on August 3 at the age of 80 after a short illness, surrounded by family.

His body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale on Thursday, August 20, from 3pm to 5pm for those wishing to pay their respects. Following this, a vigil mass will take place at Salford Cathedral at 7pm, marking the reception of his body.

The funeral service is scheduled for 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at Salford Cathedral. Mourners are encouraged to wear bow ties, which, along with his trademark Wellington boots, became synonymous with the beloved entertainer.

Jimmy Cricket was a prominent figure in the comedy scene during the 1970s and was a dedicated supporter of local charities and causes in Rochdale, where he resided.
